item.title: Status of the status page
item.author: webmaster@rapidcow.org
item.description:
So turns out maintaining a simple status page with two mere HTML pages and an XML page, whose process of updating has long been automated by Perl scripts and Template Toolkit... isn't 'simple' in the slightest. My goal with writing this, however, is not so you would pity me. I've been pretty selfish doing what I want to do, mostly unrelated to the web sites, and almost never related to school. It's like um... how you hear certain people partying in their room after the finals are over, except if you walk over there and tell them "hey, you might want to take a break..." you are greeted with a firm and adamant stubbornness of insisting that they're doing the right thing.

… which I'm not saying that I think I am. I know I've been staying on my bed with just my laptop for a week or so now. I know it's probably best that I live like a normal person more, which hopefully means I can go to sleep early and not feel sleepy after being awake for only a few hours. … and i guess i feel sorry for letting mom worry……. I just don't know when I'll get things done if not… now. Things move so fast, before I know it I'd be back—and I definitely can't return with my phone still at full storage! (And uh, my obsession with getting everything figured out and resolved at the same time I come across them =n=)

But well... personal rant aside, today is supposedly the last day of December (by the way the time just hit midnight as i was finishing up the first paragraph, but you probably knew what time that, everyone probably tells you about it... the Earth made a full cycle around the Sun, and everyone just got a year older (at least if you are Chinese)... It's not like I don't know it's 2025 that's kind of why I am writing this but it's also not like the whole point, plus it just so happens to be a year or so since rapidcow.org has been up! so i can finally do some analysis of the web traffic- okay you know what it KIND OF has to do with that it's 2025…)

*ahem* sorry—AS I WAS SAYING THOUGH it's the end of a month, end of a year too (not a very happy year for me bu- ok I need to stop going off the track), and this status page (or pages if you will) went through THREE different hosts. Like, that's INSANE! The second part was kind of my fault though, but I'll get to all of that here. (Oh, and I feel obliged to say this… This update will be a bit technical, but I feel like I should respect your choice to learn more about what happens, rather than hide those away from you. If you dislike the technical bits, then it's alright, but then I hope you can see kind of the whole point of this post is… to explain the technical stuff. That is the powerhouse of a website, the web server, the host… and what I use to make sure that everything is running (unless your ISP bans foreign websites—sorry, I don't think I have the knowledge to deal with that yet… :c))

First off you may have noticed that the "hosted by codeberg" part is not at all accurate, and, indeed if you try to access pages.status.rapidcow.codeberg.page (where the old CNAME record pointed to), you would find that the 4xx error is still there:

$ openssl s_client -crlf -nocommands -connect pages.status.rapidcow.codeberg.page:443
Connecting to 217.197.91.145
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=2 C=US, O=Internet Security Research Group, CN=ISRG Root X1
verify return:1
depth=1 C=US, O=Let's Encrypt, CN=R10
verify return:1
depth=0 CN=*.codeberg.page
verify return:1
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:CN=*.codeberg.page
   i:C=US, O=Let's Encrypt, CN=R10
   a:PKEY: rsaEncryption, 2048 (bit); sigalg: RSA-SHA256
   v:NotBefore: Nov 12 04:21:52 2024 GMT; NotAfter: Feb 10 04:21:51 2025 GMT
 1 s:C=US, O=Let's Encrypt, CN=R10
   i:C=US, O=Internet Security Research Group, CN=ISRG Root X1
   a:PKEY: rsaEncryption, 2048 (bit); sigalg: RSA-SHA256
   v:NotBefore: Mar 13 00:00:00 2024 GMT; NotAfter: Mar 12 23:59:59 2027 GMT
---
Server certificate
subject=CN=*.codeberg.page
issuer=C=US, O=Let's Encrypt, CN=R10
---
New, TLSv1.3, Cipher is TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
Protocol: TLSv1.3
---
read R BLOCK
### To make the following text easier to read, the input
### (what *I* typed into the terminal) is prefixed with
### "<<<", and the output (what the *server* sent back)
### is prefixed with ">>>".  These "###" are comments that
### clearly do not exist in the HTTP request (input) or
### the HTTP response (output).
<<< GET / HTTP/1.1
<<< Host: status.rapidcow.org
<<< Connection: close
<<<
>>> HTTP/1.1 424 Failed Dependency
>>> Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8
>>> Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin
>>> Server: pages-server
>>> Date: Tue, 31 Dec 2024 17:01:31 GMT
>>> Connection: close
>>>
>>> <!doctype html>
>>> <html class="codeberg-design">
>>>   <head>
>>>     <meta charset="utf-8" />
>>>     <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width" />
>>>     <title>Failed Dependency</title>
>>> [STYLESHEET OMITTED]
>>>   </head>
>>>   <body>
>>> [SVG THINGY OMITTED]
>>>     <h1 class="mb-0 text-primary">Failed Dependency (Error 424)!</h1>
>>>     <h5 class="text-center" style="max-width: 25em">
>>>       <p>Sorry, but this page couldn't be served:</p>
>>>       <p><b>"could not obtain repo owner from custom domain"</b></p>
>>> [HELP TEXT OMITTED]
>>>     </h5>
>>> [FOOTER OMITTED]
>>>   </body>
>>> </html>
closed

Frankly, this isn't exactly the same as accessing through status.rapidcow.org with the domain name (I believe somewhere in the SSL handshake the client sends the domain name so the server would return the correct certificate—which was the reason I was able to host multiple domains yet have separate SSLs sent back for each), but if we assume the underlying HTTP server just looks at the Host header in the HTTP request I send (judging by my other site hosted on Codeberg Pages this seems to be the case), suffice it to say that I have reliably produced what would have happened if I switched back to Codeberg now. Plus playing with the DNS record just for this experiment would be too silly, so reasonably I decided not to… but instead play this trick to get around the mismatching SSL certificate name (FYI, subdomain certificates with a CN entry like what I got above with "CN=*.codeberg.page" are only one-level deep, so an Internet-standard abiding client would deem it invalid—see third section of RFC2818 for reference. On the other hand, s_client is just an SSL client, so it doesn't validate that consistency, and I can still send an HTTP request in spite of all that. :)

So that is the state of Codeberg Pages now… I couldn't get it to work back when I still ran on it, and I don't think I will. :( But maybe stepping away is a good thing: Codeberg Pages is maintained by one person, I feel that I shouldn't asking them to look into this minute problem…

Then well, I don't know how many of you noticed that somewhat unsettling red-text at the bottom of the page—well for a while (a few weeks up until about a day ago) I hosted this on the same server where I put the funny-looking maintenance pages for rapidcow.org and friends, and also that initial version of rapidcow.org with the home page full with GIF… you know which server I am talking about. It's the one I rented from Digital Ocean since like February. 164.90.136.30—you might recognize it from that IPv4 address, even. (If not, try to dig A rapidcow.org sometime later ;)

It was quite frantic when I migrated—I archived the nginx logs, had to remove the existing nginx configs (because the maintenance pages would go up again and I don't want that to happen), then used rsync(1) to push the files, created a server config that simply served the files using try_files; then I swapped out the CNAME record for an A record, waited for it to propogate, ran certbot to issue SSL certificates for my status subdomain, then finally tweaked the nginx config slightly to my liking (I keep separate logs for port 80 (HTTP) and port 443 (HTTPS) for no reason… right :/)

But everything was fine! except people (or I guess bots) immediately started to access my other sites like rapidcow.org and www.yizx.net whose DNS records still pointed to this server! I don't know if anyone got spooked by the bad Host header error I let nginx send back… but that's what I made nginx do when no config matches. Still I thought it could be confusing to get a 4xx error instead of a 5xx one, so instead of being the responsible sysadmin to configure new nginx server blocks to do just that I removed the DNS records for my domains so that people wouldn't make the connection in the first place… (to this day if you run dig A rapidcow.org you would get nothing, which is… kind of sad, and I do apologize for that :c)

But back to the server. Something went morbidly wrong when I tried to install ubuntu-desktop on the server last night (I wanted to see how this "X11 forwarding" thing I've heard worked over SSH… for no good reason u_u): The server stopped connecting to the Internet. I couldn't install or update with apt-get, I couldn't ping(1) any domain (heck they wouldn't even resolve in the first place)—but worst of all… I couldn't log into it from my laptop via SSH. This meant that in the past few hours I had been using the Web console provided by Digital Ocean (the so-called "Rescue console", but that's only because the other console hang since the server was basically offline and the rescue console is the console that interacts with the server on the private network locally).

Now, know that I'm not saying that the server files got corrupted. It was purely a network problem which may have been caused by ubuntu-desktop (or the x2goserver I installed shortly after) was bringing its own network manager that was conflicting with the then network manager. The solution was almost trivial though: to get the Internet to work I only had to hook the eth0 interface to its gateway and subnet mask, like this:

ifconfig eth0 <ipv4 address> netmask <subnet mask> up
ip route add default via <gateway address>

The IPv4 address here is indeed the public 164.90.136.30 that you already know. These are commands were all it took to bring my server back on the Internet. And I did not have to edit /etc/resolv.conf to use Google's DNS server (8.8.8.8) because Digital Ocean's DNS servers work just fine (plus, not a lot of posts I've seen mention this, but chances are you're not supposed to edit /etc/resolv.conf directly?… mine was a symlink to a file deeply nestled inside /run/ and had a huge block of comment at the top telling me to not edit it.) But I just couldn't for the life of me figure out how to tell it to configure those on boot—as soon as I reboot all of that had to be re-run; and since SSH is busted without Internet connection, all of this could only be re-run on the rescue console… which makes things pretty annoying. >:(

I tried netplan try --debug and netplan apply --debug, and all it did was disconnect my SSH connection and never restore the IP stuff. I tried to install and re-install the cloud-init package and run dpkg-reconfigure cloud-init, checked /etc/netplan/50-cloud-init.yaml, loaded and quite possibly re-generated it with netplan, apt remove --purged and reinstalled cloud-init, landscape-common, and network-manager (since one of the complaints in /var/log/cloud-init.log was that it couldn't find NetworkManager, so I figured it could be a dependency)—it's no use. Once I reboot I end up right where I started.

Now I could continue trying by opening a support ticket on Digital Ocean, but I was tired, and it's almost new year (not like people work on new year), and things don't matter that much… so after taking out the latest nginx logs that had accumulated primarily before this disaster struck (the thing is as I said before, once the port becomes operational the logs are instantaneous—even if I finish typing in those two commands, there will be SSH login attempts, there will be HTTP requests made directly to the IP address with no Host header (likely from port scanning bots)… so a minority of logs would come after, interestingly enough) I reinstalled the whole OS. And phew it felt refreshing to see 80% of the disk space being free again… don't have to go around hunting for unused files (like I would have to for a system that I am still actively using, sigh… this feels good, honestly =v= and it's now automatically upgraded to the latest LTE of Ubuntu too!)

Of course nothing is configured yet and there shouldn't be any service running on any ports (except for sshd on port 22 because obviously I have to log in)… as to what this status page is now hosted by, well it is SourceHut! I know it sounds a lot like SourceForge, but SourceHut… to me it's like GitHub but with less clutter. Closer to Gitweb and the humble repo.or.cz (and cgit, what I once used for git.rapidcow.org), though the design looks nicer and cleaner, and it runs services that go beyond (though heavily revolve around) Git. SourceHut Pages is one such service that I really like because once you build and install this hut command guy all you have to do to get a web site up is upload a tarball and specify a domain name and… that's it. Then you point your DNS record to srht.site and it just works:

$ openssl s_client -crlf -nocommands -connect status.rapidcow.org:443
Connecting to 46.23.81.157
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=2 C=US, O=Internet Security Research Group, CN=ISRG Root X1
verify return:1
depth=1 C=US, O=Let's Encrypt, CN=E5
verify return:1
depth=0 CN=status.rapidcow.org
verify return:1
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:CN=status.rapidcow.org
   i:C=US, O=Let's Encrypt, CN=E5
   a:PKEY: id-ecPublicKey, 256 (bit); sigalg: ecdsa-with-SHA384
   v:NotBefore: Dec 31 06:39:20 2024 GMT; NotAfter: Mar 31 06:39:19 2025 GMT
 1 s:C=US, O=Let's Encrypt, CN=E5
   i:C=US, O=Internet Security Research Group, CN=ISRG Root X1
   a:PKEY: id-ecPublicKey, 384 (bit); sigalg: RSA-SHA256
   v:NotBefore: Mar 13 00:00:00 2024 GMT; NotAfter: Mar 12 23:59:59 2027 GMT
---
Server certificate
subject=CN=status.rapidcow.org
issuer=C=US, O=Let's Encrypt, CN=E5
---
New, TLSv1.3, Cipher is TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
Protocol: TLSv1.3
---
read R BLOCK
### (Same prefixes here)
<<< GET / HTTP/1.1
<<< Host: status.rapidcow.org
<<< Connection: close
<<<
>>> HTTP/1.1 200 OK
>>> Content-Length: 2742
>>> Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8
>>> Last-Modified: Tue, 31 Dec 2024 07:37:44 GMT
>>> Date: Tue, 31 Dec 2024 21:36:20 GMT
>>> Connection: close
>>>
>>> [You know the rest.... you're on it!]
closed

It even has a lot of information in the header, nice… (although I should say they are more or less inaccurate, since tarballs created by git-archive(1) all share the same timestamp that is the Commit ID =n=)

Anyways that should be it for me if not for you too ^^ Gosh is this a super long update, urgh :[ next year I might consider archiving these status updates elsewhere other than /feed.html…. but that's a job for later.:>

item.title: Winter break and stuff
item.author: webmaster@rapidcow.org
item.description:
(ouch i forgot how much tooth extraction hurts during the first few days…)

Anyway I've been having a lot of fun at home with my first ever Linux laptop! :) Staying too long in the virtual consoles, messing with Bash $PS1, learning more about TCP networking and stuff…

I also had my wisdom tooth extraction today though it hurts a lot less this time—still I don't want to risk leaving this site untouched, in case I fall ill for a day or two :( Also my mom tells me that I should rest and I think so too...

(Yeah! Web sites can wait! But health comes first! —oh and also backup backup backup backup backup—always back up never stop backing up, download your favorite things or it may be the last time you see it—backup backup BACKUP!!!)

Also: Neocities… will actually be the first to be updated, because I decided that instead of trying to make a big message, I would just… make something. I thought of this when I was walking home tonight, that the best way of showing the Web I want to see is to just make it, and its existence alone would serve to defy everything that it is different from: I like text files, not Word and PowerPoint and Excel. I like old and modest tech, not the newest buzzword AI tech. I like the 90s Web, the Open Web, not the corporate Web, where a few monopolies control all our data, creations, and livelihoods; where people are spoon-fed content made just for the sake of content, not for the love of making; and where people are compressed into canned descriptions of their lives, to be copied over and over in those perfect rectangular profile boxes, so much so that they themselves start to introduce their being as such…

……

But all of that is just what's in my head! I haven't actually written much, nyeah. :P As I said I am taking a break… a looooong break where I do things that I can never explain to any else—is it an elaborate portfolio? A programming project? A creative writing project? An ART project??? or is it just a bunch of things I like, done out of no reason other than me being the rambunctious teenage boy I am? (Well we teenagers do think alike, so umm…)

item.title: Update
item.author: webmaster@rapidcow.org
item.description:
(Old Message on Wed, 18 Dec 2024 13:29:23 -0600)

Hello hello! Good morning! ^^ (or afternoon I guess =.=)

So last night I couldn't sleep so I went though the rest of server nginx logs… stayed up quite late but in the end it was worth it I guess? At least now I get to see just how many bots are visiting and put their stats up in the hall of shame (mwehehe >:)

(New message)

Hiya so, now that I am hosting the status page myself, I can say I am quite disappointed. Within mere seconds my logs were instantaneously flooded with requests that blatantly probe for server vulnerability—paths like /.env and /wp-whatever and such. I forgot what they were exactly but they made me feel sick….

Also in case it isn't obvious enough already, every other site is still technically "down" even though the server isn't; for a while you could make requests to rapidcow.org and it would just give you a bad host error (because I disabled all my old configs and naturally nginx wouldn't recognize any virtual host other than status.rapidcow.org.) To prevent that confusion I have since removed DNS records that pointed rapidcow.org and www.rapidcow.org to my server, so now you get an DNS error instead of a scary bad host error. I haven't done that for all domains though; but I'm tired…

About the plans? Forget about it… I need to rest my eyes…. My flight back home is in less than 48 hours. I can probably look to measures to ban these bots more effectively than directly looking at the access logs (grep'ing their IPs in existing blacklists is an idea). But I won't be updating this until I'm back home….

(Sorry, it's just… the dead Internet thing feels too real. Maybe only now am I seeing it for what it is. Why did I want to make a website again? Maybe I can just turn it off when I'm tired and turn it back on when I'm not… It feels like no one's there… (or maybe I could just switch to Neocities so I don't have to experience despair from staring at the abysmal amount of bot requests))

item.title: I need more time :(
item.author: webmaster@rapidcow.org
item.description:
Yeah, I definitely underestimated what could happen over a day rather than how long it practically takes to do the thing. You never know what will get in the way. And eating more than I wanted definitely did not help my stomach, aeugh... (they even got me the wrong bao and I couldn't even complain :<)

(Life tip: if you do not want to eat more than a bowl of noodles and you see people ordering a bunch of things, *do not* order more than that bowl of noodles! Otherwise -- well there is no otherwise; you'll just suffer...)

Also I have an exam in 30 minutes it's computer science but they ask annoying questions that I don't know if I will get right, then there's math tomorrow that I think I will need to pay a little more attention to... I don't know there's just so much to do!!! >n<

But I did write a something that made updating this feed easier? I pushed that new branch to Codeberg yesterday, so you can see how it's done (THIS IS NOW GONE.) It uses Perl which I think is an underrated language full of code written by people who enjoy the craft. Really— I was reading Template::Tutorials::Datafile and many other perldocs yesterday. I am really glad to see this art isn't lost to time and completely displaced by huge corporate codebases. :)

(Every time I say something that doesn't really have to do with the announcement, haha... but this is my website! It's kind of the point that I get to talk about what I want to talk about. XD)

Oh right, and if I were to name a new time.... Let's try Wednesday in my time alright :) We'll see how things go...

item.title: Extended Maintenance
item.author: webmaster@rapidcow.org
item.description:
Argh can't believe it's 24-hours already... sorry. :( I wasn't doing just the web site thing. It's just I've never had this much free time, I had to catch up with some backing up personal stuff, and that involved hours of yelling at git-annex to stop being so paranoid about copying and deleting my files from Google Drive... and connecting a ton of cables on my bed because some of the files were only on my hard drive, yikes >_>

But I did get a look at the server logs in the end! I do have some experience exporting since I've done that before (a month or so ago), but because it was so tedious last time that I decided to "speed up" the process by making my Bash scripts more robust, and that meant running into more quirky stuff like variable scopes.

And I got up at 5 PM! Okay don't judge me I know I slept for 12 hours >:( it was more than what I expected too, but I am sort of hungry now... so I might have to go and eat something first before continuing.

Also, the CSS for this page is kind of bad: pure white on black/black on white? Old-school terminals used pure white exclusively for BOLD text (it looks something like this); it's like they understand color theory or something! So I might have to change that -- but that's only after I get the sites back up again? Waaahhh I don't knoooow >n<

-- but I know the old blue maintenance page has to go! I thought it'd mostly be the crawlers visiting (so the PNG drawing wouldn't be requested as much), but I fed the 1.5 million logs I exported last time into GoAccess and turns out there were still so many requests for the image! So the new page will have to be MUCH more lightweight (with NO images!) and I don't know, maybe I will call it an "under construction" page to distinguish it from what I am calling maintenance for this ongoing... thing?

But yeah. I will need more time. It'll probably take more than a day to get everything done, but at least I will configure nginx properly this time, set up logrotate and figure out how to export logs in a way that doesn't shut all the ports down again like this, put up the new page for every site that I'm not ready to show -- geesh does that not sound like a lot to you? Being a webmaster is HARD. :c

BUT... it's a battle I am willing to fight. Being a webmaster is fun, even if I know that fewer people will watching compared to when I was on YouTube or Twitter. Having said that I do remember reading a few things that I quite liked: this world needs more webmasters, not influencers, TikToks, social media -- and I definitely don't mean graphic designers and developers!

Yeah right this announcement has been long enough I'll go eat something and then get back to work =n= (ooh and I'm also thinking of publishing some stats from my nginx logs, with individual IP addresses anonymized (obviously)! If you have anything specific you want to see in mind (yes! YOU reading this!!!) send me an e-mail (it's in this RSS feed) and let me know! Otherwise I'll only look into my favorite stats like how much bandwidth I am wasting...)

item.title: Server Downtime [+24 hours]
item.author: webmaster@rapidcow.org
item.description:
Hi this is rapid!

It's been a while since i cleaned out the nginx logs, now that my finals are out of the way [well, the hard ones for me at least :] But before I do that I prefer to not have to worry about new logs coming in. Stuff like telling nginx where to write the access/error logs and logrotate are going to create a mess if I don't set them up right...

So I decided to schedule a DOWNTIME! Basically, the server will be down for real this time (there wouldn't even be a maintenance page). This affects all sites besides this status and the URL shortener (a.rdks.org), which are the only sites hosted by Codeberg Pages. Though I think no one would be seriously affected by this, so I won't give you too much time prepare.

Things I want to do besides exporting nginx logs include:

  1. set www.rapidcow.org as the canonical domain
  2. clean up my server files scattered over /home and /var/www/ (and update the nginx rules, obviously)
  3. and probably learn how to use logrotate so that I'm not looking at thousands of lines at once... also i want to see how i can do this more regularly and easily (and maybe even get GoAccess to work?)

The exact period of maintenance is... I'm not sure. But the plan is that it would be back within 24 hours of the publish date of this post (so Sat thru Sun, UTC 2 AM). The HTTP(S) ports might get turned on and off during this period (so don't be surprised if you see the sites still running -- I might still be working!) If I need more time than that, I'll let you know :)

Thank you for understanding. It's an honor to be your host of my Web... o7 -RC

item.title: Plans for the end of 2024
item.author: webmaster@rapidcow.org
item.description:
I got some more motivation to return to this and escape social media hellhole! Thank you to my anonymous friend for being my FIRST subscriber outside of social media :)

The plans are simple: www.rapidcow.org will get a landing page and a home page and www.endfind.me will get just a landing page that double as the home page. (Don't visit either yet though, and if you do, don't be like Twitter.)

The exact date I'm unsure, but it should happen sometime between next week and the week after. I'll let you know that when that happens. Before that though I need to deal with them finals next week (ugh school... DX)

Thanks. I hope I can keep feeling this motivated.

item.title: Update: Neocities
item.author: webmaster@rapidcow.org
item.description:
I made a Neocities account and wrote more than I ever intended to even for www.rapidcow.org o_o

Looks like signing up for Neocities was the right choice, but well, now I'm exhausted… and I need some sleep….

(if you are curious about it now, head over to https://rapidcow.neocities.org. i sat in front of my laptop for ~4 hours just to write up a good-enough answer — i did NOT expect it to go like this.)
